entries.subject: Schenk 2020 Voyager corrected mosaic
entries.finding: The losslessly retained mumap-cyl-180180.cub supplies Monochrome on its 240 m simple-cylindrical grid. It retains source photomet normalization, seams, camera marks, cast shadows and missing coverage; the 0–2400 DN stretch is display-only.

entries.subject: Schenk 2020 merged Miranda DEM
entries.finding: The losslessly retained mudem-ZT-cyl.cub supplies Elevation: merged stereogrammetry and photoclinometry in kilometres above the published ellipsoid. Its 240 m grid, source errors, smooth patches and missing samples do not establish uniform terrain accuracy.

entries.subject: Thomson and Baynham 2026 digitized historical map
entries.finding: The CC BY 4.0 GIS release supplies the historical Geology dataset after its incompatible page CRS was reconstructed with six Miranda graticule fit intersections, six withheld intersections and three crater checks. It represents Voyager-era unit interpretation, not composition or terrain; coverage is about 44.2% and degree-scale registration limits remain.

entries.subject: JPL ura5vuu2.tif simulator map
entries.finding: The 1440 × 720 simulator display map is superseded by the denser Schenk mosaic and is not retained as a duplicate Monochrome dataset.
entries.revisitWhen: A JPL release supplies a higher-detail, source-controlled Miranda map with documented projection and processing that improves on the selected Schenk mosaic.

entries.subject: PIA01490 south-polar and color press images
entries.finding: The press mosaics were examined as rendered-disc or press imagery; they do not establish a reusable registered surface map or global color coverage.
entries.revisitWhen: A primary release provides the underlying Miranda observations with reusable terms, body-fixed geometry and coverage adequate for independent registration.

entries.subject: USGS Miranda Voyager control network
entries.finding: The USGS control network is retained as registration support for the selected sources, not as a separate image or measured-scalar dataset.

entries.subject: Historical geology registration limit
entries.finding: The retained 1.3–3.3 degree landmark differences are independent checks, not uncertainty bounds for every geological boundary; ambiguous source layer combinations remain missing.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-controlled Miranda geological release or additional independently identified controls can improve the page-to-body registration without converting source annotations or Z values into terrain.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 ISS green/violet/ultraviolet color frames
entries.finding: 3 GEOMED frames in 1 complete sets (1.1 km per pixel) placed by limb fit and mosaic registration supply the Voyager color dataset. Whole-disc violet/green and ultraviolet/green are tied to Bell and McCord (1991) Fig. 2 (1.03, 1.06); the archive calibration gives 0.927 and 1.056. No phase normalisation; the north stays unavailable.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Helfenstein, Veverka and Thomas (1988) fitted Hapke models to Voyager whole-disc photometry of the five large Uranian moons. Only the abstract could be read (single-scattering albedo from 0.3 for Umbriel to 0.7 for Ariel, g near -0.3), and a whole-disc fit states no emission range. The summary of Hillier, Helfenstein and Veverka in NASA's Reports of Planetary Geology and Geophysics Program 1987 (TM-4041) is open: Minnaert parameters fitted to Voyager clear-filter images (0.48 micrometres) at 13 to 43 degrees phase, with the global k ranging from about 0.6 at 13 degrees to about 0.8 at 43 degrees, nearly independent of wavelength, and no Voyager data below 13 degrees. Two rounded end values are not a law: the k at each phase is in the closed paper (Hillier et al. 1989), and nothing constrains the flood-lit view at zero phase. Schenk's 2020 mosaic history names ISIS photomet without its parameter file. Miranda keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: The Minnaert k at each phase, or a Hapke fit with its ranges, is read in Hillier et al. (1989), or the photometric parameter file of Schenk's mosaic is released.

entries.subject: Surface map left edge after the raster lane change
entries.finding: The raster lane writes this map from 0° E, but surface-map.json still declared the retired atlas's 180° E left edge, so the globe, labels and status-bar longitude were half a turn from the imagery. Read through its georeferenced source, the prepared normal map correlates 0.88 from 0° E and 0.03 from 180° E. The declaration is now 0° E, and preparation refuses a declared edge the source contradicts.
